contract_plain_english: The source prints the monotonicity assertion ∥X∥Lp≤∥X∥Lq for any random variable X and every 0≤p≤q≤∞ [printed p.6, Equation (1.3)]. But its preceding finite-exponent definition is (E|X|^p)^(1/p) only for p>0, and it separately defines only the p=∞ endpoint [printed p.5]. Thus the printed p=0 case has no source-defined L0 meaning, and the accompanying Jensen explanation also fails there because it uses q/p [printed p.6]. The source therefore contains a genuine endpoint obstruction: zero is unquestionably printed, but no supplied definition or proof makes that endpoint a well-defined claim. Restricting the theorem to 0<p≤q≤∞ would be an inferred correction, not the exact printed contract.
